Let \(M\) be the maximum value of the product of two positive integers when their sum is 66 . Let the sample space \(S=\left\{x \in Z: x(66-x) \geq \frac{5}{9} M\right\}\) and the event \(A=\{x \in S: x\) is a multiple of 3\(\}\). Then \(P(A)\) is equal to

questions.explanation:
For positive integers with sum \(66\), the product is maximum when the integers are \(33\) and \(33\).

\(\Rightarrow M=33^2=1089\)

The condition for \(S\) is \(\displaystyle x(66-x)\geq\dfrac59(1089)=605\).

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow x^2-66x+605\leq0\)

\(\Rightarrow (x-11)(x-55)\leq0\)

\(\Rightarrow 11\leq x\leq55\)

The set \(S\) contains \(55-11+1=45\) integers.

The multiples of \(3\) in this interval are \(12,15,\ldots,54\).

Their number is \(\displaystyle \dfrac{54-12}{3}+1=15\).

\(\Rightarrow P(A)=\dfrac{15}{45}=\dfrac13\)

The correct option is B.
